origins: Wheelchairs, walkers, slow movement, and special needs can make us feel obstructive in crowded places, in families, and in plans. Sighs, glances, and inaccessible spaces reinforce this.
teaches: Jesus welcomed the disabled and the marginalized. He said to invite “the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind,” and Scripture shows people making room for them. “God settles the lonely in families.” “Each member belongs to one another.” Inaccessible spaces are failures of the community, not of you. God’s people are called to make room. You belong, and you can say what you need.
self_statements: Everything has to change for me.
People wish I were not here.
I take up too much space.
errors: Believing I either fit in perfectly or I am in the way.
Predicting that I will always be an obstacle.
Feeling awkward and concluding that I am unwelcome.
questions: What places or groups are accessible and kind?
What do I need in order to participate, and can I ask for it?
What does Scripture say about those with disabilities?
How do I feel when someone else asks for help?
What gifts do I bring to a gathering?
truth: I belong. God places the lonely in families, and Jesus welcomes everyone. I can ask for what I need, choose welcoming places, and offer my gifts.
hw_truths: God settles the lonely in families.
I can ask for what I need.
log: Each week, note one place or person where you felt welcome.
actions: Write where you feel at ease.
prayer: Lord, I feel in the way. Thank You that You welcome everyone. Lead me to people who make room and use my gifts among them. Amen.
